spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Encoding every derivative by a recursively generated polynomial turns analytic remainder control into coefficient-norm bookkeeping that is also algorithmically executable.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Writing f^(m)=P_m exp(2πicy^3+2πixy) gives a recursion for P_m and a norm bound; when |cK^2|≤1/48, M=ceil(8log(K/ε)) makes the Euler-Maclaurin remainder below ε, and derivatives are computable in O((m+j+1)^2) operations.
directed.conceptual_reading: The same recursive representation proves both small error and bounded computational cost.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Polynomial P_m is the bridge from oscillatory derivatives to finite arithmetic and norm estimates.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The certification depends on bounded x, small cK^2, K>Λ, and O(ν^2)-bit arithmetic.
directed.uncertainty: Low to moderate; the recurrence is legible, while exact norm constants are formula-dependent.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Correction integrals are split by frequency: nearly resonant terms are locally expanded, while nonresonant terms are integrated explicitly and converted to weighted quadratic sums.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Lemma 5.3 expands the derivative corrections into integrals of x^l exp(2πiτx)F(K;a+αx,b), splits indices at |τ+αk|=2l+2, uses Taylor expansion in the small-frequency part, and explicit antiderivatives in the large-frequency part.
directed.conceptual_reading: Frequency localization selects the representation in which either smoothness or denominator decay is available.
directed.representation_or_bridge: After an index shift limits cancellation, rationally weighted exponential sums reduce through the prior machinery to ordinary quadratic sums.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The result relies on |cK1^2|<1/48, bounded parameter ranges, sufficient precision, and Theorem 2.1 rather than proving a standalone evaluator.
directed.uncertainty: Moderate because formulas (5.12)-(5.15) are dense, though the split and reduction are clear.
